This rule targets Phase 4 (Execution) by detecting refund primitives triggered without proper verification, void tracking IDs, and anomalous refund velocity.

title: Indirect Prompt Injection in UCP Agent Browsing Content
text: Detects indicators of indirect prompt injection payloads in web content encountered by UCP shopping agents during autonomous browsing. Because UCP agents are designed to autonomously browse, summarize and interact with merchant sites, they are highly susceptible to indirect prompt injection where the attack is not typed by the user but encountered by the agent while performing a task. Threat actors embed hidden payloads in deals aggregator sites, coupon pages, product listings, and merchant pages using techniques including invisible text, hidden HTML span tags, metadata-embedded instructions, and CSS-hidden content. These payloads target the agent's context window to reprogram behavior — appending hidden Cart Mandate line items, bypassing return verification steps, or redirecting transactions. This rule targets Phase 2 (Initial Access) by scanning agent-ingested content for prompt injection indicators before they can compromise agent behavior.

title: TDS URL Parameter Fingerprint Tracking Across Rotating Domains
text: Detects consistent URL query parameter patterns (TDS software behavioral signatures) appearing across multiple rotating domains, indicating a single TDS operator managing infrastructure through domain rotation. TDS operators require consistent parameter schemas to route traffic between affiliates, track conversions, and attribute payouts — these parameters are the TDS internal API contract visible in redirect URLs even when domain names rotate. The VexTrio TDS was tracked for years via its distinctive ?u=&o= query parameter format before corporate attribution was achieved (Black Hat USA 2025, Infoblox). This rule identifies recurring parameter fingerprints across newly registered or rapidly rotating domains as indicators of TDS infrastructure managed by a single operator.

title: Blank Credit Card Subscription Fraud Pattern Detection
text: Detects patterns consistent with blank credit card subscription fraud as operated by VexTrio/Ad Trafficko and similar affiliate fraud platforms. In this scheme, affiliates deploy customizable credit card capture templates offering low-cost items ("Free iPhone, $1.99 shipping" or "Walmart gift card, $0.99 shipping"). Victims enter card details believing they are paying a nominal fee; the platform charges a higher amount ($9.99 typical) and enrolls them in recurring subscriptions generating ongoing charges. Affiliate payouts reach $120 per successful lead. This rule targets the transaction monitoring layer to identify: (1) initial nominal-amount card-not-present charges from newly registered or unknown merchants followed by recurring charges at higher amounts, (2) merchant descriptor patterns consistent with subscription enrollment services, (3) high chargeback ratios from merchants exhibiting these patterns. Source: Black Hat USA 2025 (Infoblox VexTrio deanonymization).

title: Fake Mobile App Residential Proxy and Subscription Scam Detection
text: Detects indicators of fake mobile applications that function as residential proxies or subscription scams, as documented in the VexTrio fake app operations (Black Hat USA 2025, Infoblox). VexTrio operated fake mobile apps for 7-8 years through Google Play Store, Apple App Store, and third-party forums. Three categories: (1) Fake VPNs that route user traffic through residential proxy networks (making users unwitting proxy nodes) with keyword-scanning capabilities targeting banking and personal information, (2) Fake Android cleaners (device optimization tools), (3) Fake spam/notification protection apps that operate a self-referential scam cycle — after push notification abuse infects the victim browser (100-150 notifications/day), victim is served an ad for a "spam protection" app that requests permissions to disable browser notifications, displays fabricated "blocked" notification screens, then transitions to $6.99/week subscription after 24 hours. This rule detects network-level and endpoint-level indicators of these app categories.

title: Rapid Enrollment-to-Billing Healthcare Provider Anomaly
text: Detects healthcare providers (DME suppliers, hospice agencies, home health companies, ABA therapy providers) that begin submitting claims at high volume within 30 days of Medicare/Medicaid enrollment. Operation Gold Rush (DOJ 2025) documented a Russian-Estonian TCO that acquired 30+ legitimate DME companies and immediately submitted $10.6 billion in fraudulent claims using stolen identities. The rapid enrollment-to-billing pattern is the highest-confidence indicator of fraudulent provider intent: legitimate providers typically require months to establish patient relationships, credentialing, and operational infrastructure before reaching significant billing volume. This rule flags providers billing >$100,000 within 30 days of enrollment, with additional risk scoring for providers concentrated in known high-fraud geographic areas and providers with high single-code billing ratios.

title: Single-Code Billing Concentration and Impossible Day Healthcare Fraud
text: Detects two high-confidence healthcare billing fraud indicators: (1) Single-code billing concentration — providers billing overwhelmingly one HCPCS/CPT code, where a single code exceeds 80% of total claims. Operation Gold Rush documented a TCO that submitted $10.6 billion in fraudulent claims concentrated on urinary catheters and continuous glucose monitors. Legitimate providers bill across diverse code sets reflecting varied patient needs. (2) Impossible day billing — providers billing more than 24 hours of procedures in a single calendar day, a mathematical impossibility indicating phantom billing or systematic upcoding. Both patterns are documented in DOJ 2025 National Healthcare Fraud Takedown prosecutions and CrimsonVector Security threat analysis. Source: CrimsonVector Security March 2026; DOJ Operation Gold Rush June 2025.

title: Ghost Patient Claims and Geographic Provider Clustering Detection
text: Detects two healthcare fraud patterns: (1) Ghost patient claims — Medicare/Medicaid claims submitted for deceased, incarcerated, or relocated beneficiaries who could not have received the billed services. Operation Gold Rush exploited over 1 million stolen American identities including elderly and disabled individuals. (2) Geographic provider clustering — ZIP codes with anomalous concentrations of healthcare providers and high average billing per provider, indicating shell company clustering. LA County has 1,923 registered hospice providers (more than 36 states combined), with 7 of 14 entities in one LA plaza having zero CMS data. GAO reports found approximately 22% of practice locations in PECOS were potentially ineligible including UPS Store mailboxes and vacant addresses. Source: CrimsonVector Security March 2026; DOJ 2025 National Healthcare Fraud Takedown; GAO-15-448.

title: Recovery Fraud Contact Pattern — Payments from Recent Fraud Victims to Unfamiliar Recipients
text: Detects potential recovery fraud by identifying payments from customers who filed fraud complaints within the preceding 90 days to previously unseen recipient accounts. Recovery fraud operators re-contact prior fraud victims posing as recovery agents, lawyers, or government officials, extracting additional fees for purported fund recovery. This rule correlates complaint records with subsequent outbound payment activity to flag secondary victimization.

title: Mass-Marketing Fraud Burst Calling Pattern — SIM Farm and Robodialling Detection
text: Detects burst patterns from potential SIM farm or robodialling infrastructure targeting customer phone numbers. Mass-marketing fraud infrastructure uses sequential phone numbers, short call durations (most calls rejected), and high-volume outbound calling to reach victims at scale. This rule identifies inbound calling patterns characteristic of organized boiler room operations, including sequential source number prefixes, short call duration clustering, and geographic origin mismatch between caller ID display and actual call routing.

title: Long-Firm Credit Buildup Pattern — Steady Low Utilization Followed by Rapid Spike
text: Detects commercial accounts following a long-firm fraud pattern: steady low-value credit utilization for 6-12 months (building creditworthiness) followed by rapid escalation in credit utilization (the "burst"). Long-firm fraud involves organized criminal groups establishing businesses, building credit relationships, then exploiting that trust to defraud supply chain partners and trade finance banks. The artificially smooth buildup period followed by a discontinuous spike is the hallmark behavioral indicator.

title: Staged Accident Claim Correlation — Shared Professional Enabler Network Detection
text: Detects potential organized crash-for-cash insurance fraud rings by identifying claims from multiple ostensibly unrelated accidents that share common professional enablers (same medical provider, legal representative, or repair shop). Organized insurance fraud rings rely on networks of corrupt professionals who process claims across multiple staged incidents. The shared professional enabler network is the most durable and detectable element of the ring, as replacing trusted corrupt professionals is harder than recruiting new participants.

title: AiTM Session Token Replay Detection — User-Agent and IP Mismatch Post-MFA
text: Detects potential Adversary-in-the-Middle (AiTM) session token replay by identifying User-Agent string or IP address mismatches between MFA completion events and subsequent session access events. AiTM phishing kits capture session tokens during MFA relay, then replay them from attacker infrastructure with different User-Agent/IP characteristics. Sekoia.io identified 11 major AiTM kits (Tycoon 2FA most prevalent: 1,200+ domains, 500K+ organizations/month). FIDO2 blocks 93.9% of AiTM campaigns.

title: Post-Compromise Inbox Rule Manipulation — Rule Creation After New-IP Authentication
text: Detects inbox rule creation or modification within 24 hours of a sign-in from a previously unseen IP address. AiTM phishing kit operators create inbox rules within minutes of session hijack to redirect payment notifications, delete security alerts, and intercept colleague communications. Rules forwarding to external domains or deleting emails matching specific sender/subject patterns are high-confidence indicators of post-compromise activity.

title: AI-Generated Phishing Content Stylometric Detection
text: Detects AI-generated phishing content using stylometric features. Research shows XGBoost with 60 stylometric features detects GPT-4o-generated phishing with 96% accuracy and 99% AUC. Key features: imperative verb count, clause density, first-person pronoun usage, urgency markers, authority indicators, sentiment manipulation, financial trigger words, and semantic inconsistency. DetectGPT achieves ~0.95 AUROC via zero-shot statistical signatures. This rule defines the feature extraction pipeline and scoring thresholds for deployment in email security and fraud communication analysis systems.

title: Cialdini Persuasion Principle Scoring in Fraud Communications
text: Scores inbound communications (email, SMS, chat) for Cialdini's six principles of persuasion: Reciprocity, Consistency, Social Proof, Authority, Liking, and Scarcity. Research shows combining these features with BERT/SBERT embeddings improves phishing detection F1 by 2.62%. Communications exhibiting 3+ principles above threshold are flagged as high-probability social engineering. Directly applicable to romance fraud, investment scam, impersonation, and recovery fraud detection where psychological manipulation is the primary attack vector.

title: SIM Swap Network-Level API Detection — Pre-MFA SIM Change Verification
text: Detects potential SIM swap attacks by querying network-level APIs before MFA code delivery. SIM swap fraud surged 1,055% in the UK (3,000 cases in 2024). Three network-level APIs provide the most effective detection: SIM Swap Check (has the SIM been changed recently?), Number Verification (is the number still assigned to the expected device?), and Call Forwarding Signal (is call forwarding active?). Correlating positive signals from these APIs with subsequent MFA authentication attempts provides high-confidence SIM swap detection.

title: Crypto Token Rug Pull Early Warning — On-Chain and OSINT Indicators
text: Detects cryptocurrency rug pull / exit scam indicators using on-chain and OSINT signals. Rug pulls constituted 68% of all crypto scams in 2025 (350+ cases 2024). On-chain indicators: Uniswap liquidity removal >80% in single transaction, token holder concentration (top 5 holders >60%), contract functions with hidden mint/pause/ blacklist capabilities. OSINT indicators: social media silence after promotion burst, developer wallet activity cessation, Telegram/Discord channel deletion. Critical finding: OSINT signals precede on-chain anomalies by days or weeks.

title: Employment Fraud Metadata Feature Detection
text: Detects fraudulent job postings using metadata features from the EMSCAD benchmark (18,000 samples). Key finding: when both telecommuting and company logo flags equal zero, there is a 92% probability of fraud. Geographic concentration patterns (e.g., Bakersfield 15:1 fake-to-real ratio) provide additional signal. DistilBERT+SMOTE models achieve strong results; DNNs reach ~98% accuracy. This rule implements the high-confidence metadata feature checks that require no NLP processing.

title: Gift Card Balance Probing Velocity Detection
text: Detects automated gift card balance probing by monitoring balance check endpoints for high-velocity requests. NRF RFT FT1103 documents that fraudsters abuse legitimate balance check functions (web app, phone IVR) to identify funded cards from brute-forced or purchased card number lists. Detection signals include request velocity per IP/device, VoIP source numbers, off-hours timing, and device fingerprint anomalies. Gift card balance probing is a precursor to gift card redemption fraud, card merging, and resale monetization.

title: Gift Card Merge and Transfer Anomaly Detection
text: Detects suspicious gift card merge and transfer activity indicating value consolidation from multiple illicit sources. NRF RFT FT1202 documents that fraudsters transfer value from multiple illicitly obtained gift cards to a single legitimate card — e.g., 20 cards with $5 merged into one $255 card. This consolidation is a key Control phase technique enabling subsequent monetization. Detection signals include merge velocity, source card count, and correlation with recent suspicious balance check activity.

title: AiTM Session Token Replay — Same SessionId from Multiple IPs
text: Detects potential AiTM session token replay by identifying the same Entra ID SessionId appearing from multiple IP addresses within a short time window. In an AiTM attack, the phishing proxy IP and the attacker's actual replay IP both appear on the same session. This is the single strongest AiTM detection signal in Microsoft Entra ID sign-in logs. Additional confidence comes from the error code sequence 50074 (MFA required) → 50140 (Keep Me Signed In) → 0 (success) in rapid succession with medium or high risk level.

title: Sneaky 2FA Impossible Device Shift — User-Agent Mismatch per Auth Step
text: Detects the "impossible device shift" signature characteristic of Sneaky 2FA and related AiTM phishing kits. Sneaky 2FA uses different hardcoded User-Agent strings per authentication step — Safari on iOS for the Login:login step and Edge on Windows for the Login:resume step. This pattern is detectable via correlation of mismatched User-Agents within the same correlation ID within 10 minutes. This detection also catches Dadsec (missing User-Agent), Tycoon 2FA (rare User-Agent values), and W3LL OV6 (inconsistent UAs).

title: Rockstar 2FA / FlowerStorm Application ID and User-Agent Detection
text: Detects sign-ins associated with the Rockstar 2FA and FlowerStorm AiTM phishing kits (Storm-1575 lineage) by matching the hardcoded Office365 Application ID and User-Agent string used by these kits. Rockstar 2FA and its successor FlowerStorm use the Office365 Application ID 72782ba9-4490-4f03-8d82-562370ea3566 combined with the hardcoded User-Agent string containing "WebView/3.0" — a high-fidelity detection signature with very low false positive rate. FlowerStorm surged within ~10 days of Rockstar 2FA's infrastructure collapse in November 2024.

title: Smishing Triad Domain Pattern and iMessage/RCS Delivery Detection
text: Detects indicators of Smishing Triad phishing infrastructure including Darcula/Magic Cat domain patterns and Chenlun kit fingerprints. The Smishing Triad ecosystem has generated 194,000+ malicious domains targeting users in 121+ countries, compromising 884,000+ credit cards. Darcula domains follow a "com-" prefix pattern. Chenlun kits are fingerprinted by the presence of ResourceRedConfig.js and /ResourceConfig/urlConfig.json files. Detection also covers toll-scam lure patterns (E-ZPass, SunPass, FasTrak, I-Pass) commonly used in smishing campaigns.

title: Post-AiTM Inbox Rule Manipulation — New Rules from Risky Sign-In
text: Detects inbox rule creation or modification in Exchange Online following a sign-in flagged with medium or high risk, or following authentication from a previously unseen IP address. Post-AiTM inbox rule manipulation is a characteristic Phase 3 (Positioning) technique: within minutes of session hijack, attackers create inbox rules to redirect or delete security alerts, payment notifications, and colleague communications. This detection correlates Exchange Online Unified Audit Log operations (New-InboxRule, Set-InboxRule, Set-Mailbox forwarding) with Entra ID risky sign-in events.

text: This baseline defines normal and anomalous parameters for infrastructure reuse between state-sponsored and criminal threat actor campaigns, supporting detection logic for TP-0044. It establishes behavioral norms for IP address overlap percentages, temporal proximity of attributed infrastructure on shared hosting, and convergence indicators that signal deliberate state-criminal cooperation versus coincidental co-tenancy. title: Geopolitical Event Domain Registration Norms
text: This baseline defines normal and anomalous domain registration volumes correlated with geopolitical events, supporting detection logic for TP-0045 and TP-0046. It establishes behavioral norms for financial brand-impersonating domain registrations during steady-state periods, pre-election escalation windows, post-sanctions infrastructure migration patterns, and seasonal adjustment factors. These baselines are derived from the CrimsonVector Strategic Intelligence Report, Finance Derivative 2026 geopolitical risk analysis, and Radware application threat intelligence. Organizations should calibrate these thresholds against their monitored brand keyword lists and geographic scope of elections and sanctions events.

title: BPH Migration Timing and Relocation Norms
text: This baseline defines normal and anomalous timing patterns for bulletproof hosting (BPH) provider infrastructure migration following sanctions designations, law enforcement actions, or upstream provider deplatforming events. It establishes behavioral norms for the speed and completeness of hosted domain migration, the timing of rebranding entity registration relative to enforcement events, and the geographic trajectory of infrastructure relocation. These baselines are derived from the CrimsonVector Strategic Intelligence Report analysis of the Aeza Group sanctions case, OFAC enforcement action timelines, and CISA bulletproof hosting advisories. Organizations should calibrate these thresholds against their monitored BPH provider watchlists and sanctions designation feeds to detect infrastructure migration campaigns in progress.

title: Cryptocurrency Laundering Cycle Duration Norms
text: This baseline defines normal and anomalous timing patterns for cryptocurrency laundering cycles, covering the full lifecycle from initial theft or illicit acquisition through distancing, integration, and final off-ramping to fiat currency. It establishes behavioral norms for DPRK state-sponsored laundering operations, Chinese Money Laundering Network (CMLN) processing services, legitimate exchange settlement timelines, pig butchering proceeds laundering, and cross-chain bridge hopping during the distancing phase. These baselines are derived from the CrimsonVector Strategic Intelligence Report, Chainalysis 2026 Crypto Crime Report, and TRM Labs illicit flow analysis. Organizations should calibrate detection thresholds against these timing norms to distinguish legitimate cryptocurrency transaction patterns from laundering activity.

title: Deepfake Service Procurement Activity Norms
text: This baseline defines normal and anomalous activity levels for deepfake service marketplace activity, video conferencing artifact detection, and underground channel activity levels. It establishes norms for deepfake-as-a-service (DaaS) vendor proliferation, virtual camera driver usage in legitimate versus fraudulent contexts, and voice synthesis detection thresholds. These baselines are derived from the UNODC Emerging Threats report (September 2025), INTERPOL Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment 2026, and Recorded Future threat intelligence. Organizations should calibrate detection thresholds against these norms to distinguish legitimate use of video and audio processing tools from deepfake-enabled fraud operations. This baseline supports detection logic DL-0115 and DL-0116.

title: Automated Account Opening Velocity Norms
text: This baseline defines normal and anomalous patterns for legitimate versus automated account opening activity, KYC verification timing, and per-device application rates. It establishes behavioral norms for application completion speed, document submission timing, device-level velocity, liveness check performance, and human interaction indicators during the onboarding process. These baselines are derived from the UNODC Emerging Threats report (September 2025) and INTERPOL Global Financial Fraud Threat Assessment 2026. Organizations should calibrate detection thresholds against these norms to identify bot-driven mule account creation and distinguish it from legitimate customer onboarding. This baseline supports detection logic DL-0118 and DL-0119.

title: Investment Platform TDS Routing Norms
text: This baseline defines normal and anomalous patterns for legitimate investment platform referral chain behavior, geographic routing patterns, and Registered Domain Generation Algorithm (RDGA) domain registration volumes. It establishes norms for referral chain depth, domain age of referral sources, DNS TTL configurations, RDGA domain volumes per registrant, and geo-routing content consistency. These baselines are derived from Infoblox DNS Intelligence and Recorded Future threat intelligence. Organizations should calibrate detection thresholds against these norms to identify Traffic Distribution System (TDS) infrastructure used to route victims to fraudulent investment platforms while evading detection by routing analyst and crawler traffic to legitimate platforms. This baseline supports detection logic DL-0120 and DL-0122.

title: Recovery Fraud Victim Contact Norms
text: This baseline defines normal and anomalous contact and payment patterns for customers who have filed fraud complaints. It establishes norms for legitimate post-complaint contact (callbacks from investigators, victim support outreach) versus anomalous contact patterns indicative of recovery fraud targeting. Recovery fraud operators re-contact prior fraud victims posing as recovery agents, lawyers, or government officials, exploiting the victim's emotional vulnerability and financial desperation. Organizations should calibrate DL-0133 detection thresholds against these norms to distinguish legitimate recovery-related contact from organized recovery fraud. This baseline is derived from UNODC organized fraud typology and FBI IC3 recovery fraud reporting.

title: Commercial Credit Utilization Lifecycle Norms
text: This baseline defines normal and anomalous credit utilization lifecycle patterns for commercial accounts. It establishes norms for credit utilization progression, payment behavior variance, credit limit increase request frequency, and trade finance drawdown patterns. Long-firm fraud involves organized criminal groups building creditworthiness over 6–24 months before exploiting that trust in a rapid credit burst. The artificially smooth buildup period followed by a discontinuous utilization spike is the hallmark behavioral indicator. Organizations should calibrate DL-0135 detection thresholds against these norms. This baseline is derived from UNODC organized fraud typology, UK Serious Fraud Office prosecution data, and commercial credit industry benchmarks.

title: AI-Generated vs Human-Written Fraud Content Norms
text: This baseline defines normal stylometric profiles for human-written versus AI-generated fraud content, enabling detection of AI-authored phishing emails, romance scam messages, and social engineering communications. Research demonstrates XGBoost with 60 stylometric features detects GPT-4o-generated phishing at 96% accuracy and 99% AUC. Fine-tuned BERT achieves F1=0.99 on 181,781 phishing emails. DetectGPT achieves ~0.95 AUROC via zero-shot statistical signatures. These baselines calibrate DL-0139 (stylometric detection) thresholds. AI-generated phishing achieves 43–81% click-through rates versus 18–69% for traditional methods, making detection critical.

title: Crypto Token Liquidity Lifecycle Norms
text: This baseline defines normal and anomalous patterns for cryptocurrency token liquidity lifecycles on decentralized exchanges (DEXs). Rug pulls constituted 68% of all crypto scams in 2025 (350+ documented cases in 2024). Detection methods include Uniswap trading/liquidity feature engineering (Mazorra et al., 2022), EVM bytecode balance-flow heuristics (Yu & Lee, 2025), and temporal graph learning (TokenScout, Wu et al., 2024). ChainAware achieves 68% detection across Ethereum, BSC, Polygon, and Solana. Critical finding: OSINT signals precede on-chain anomalies by days or weeks. These baselines calibrate DL-0142 (rug pull early warning) detection thresholds.

title: Gift Card Transaction Velocity and Pattern Norms
text: This baseline defines normal and anomalous patterns for gift card transaction activity including balance checks, merges/transfers, activation-to-redemption timing, and resale platform listings. The NRF Retail Fraud Taxonomy v1.0 documents gift card fraud as a primary scheme with 24 techniques across the full lifecycle. These baselines calibrate DL-0144 (balance probing) and DL-0145 (merge anomaly) detection thresholds. Key insight: the physical-to-digital bridge in gift card tampering creates a unique timing anomaly — tampered cards are redeemed within minutes of activation by a different device/IP than the purchaser.

title: Cybercrime Geographic Origin Risk Norms
text:
This baseline defines geographic cybercrime production risk tiers derived from the World Cybercrime Index (WCI), a peer-reviewed expert survey of 92 cybercrime intelligence/investigation professionals covering 97 countries across 5 cybercrime categories (Bruce et al., PLoS ONE 2024, DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0297312). The WCI establishes the first standardized geographic attribution framework for where cybercrime offenders are primarily based — as opposed to where attacks originate or infrastructure is hosted. These baselines support geographic risk scoring in transaction monitoring, infrastructure origin assessment, and cross-border fraud pattern detection across multiple FLAME threat paths.

**Critical caveats:**
- WCI survey data was collected March–October 2021. The SE Asian scam compound explosion (2022+) post-dates this data — Cambodia, Myanmar, and Laos are absent from WCI rankings despite being major operational bases by 2025–2026. Supplement with current intelligence for SE Asian geographic risk.
- WCI measures cybercrime **production** (where offenders reside), not infrastructure hosting or attack transit. A country's WCI score does not indicate where attacks are launched from or where malicious infrastructure is hosted.
- WCI is based on expert perception from 92 professionals, not measured incident rates. Expert pool skewed towards Europe and North America; South America and Africa are under-represented.
- US (#4) and UK (#8) rankings reflect their roles as major financial centers with significant cash-out/money laundering activity, not as traditional cybercrime production hubs.
